Hi Dylan —

Thanks for agreeing to take a quick look. Attached is the first‑cut of our on‑prem VPC reference diagram (control/data plane separation) plus a short matrix of egress scenarios we expect from tenant runtime (forbidden, allowed via proxy, allowed direct). We want Redwood to confirm a) the control plane attachment pattern makes sense for your sidecar/KV cache traffic and b) the egress policy notation is clear for our NOC and security teams.

Quick context: TelcoGrid will run a private deployment in our colo pods with NAT egress and an edge relay. We need to avoid hairpinning for tenant data and ensure telemetry egress goes to observability endpoints over a dedicated path.

Attachments: vpc-plane-interface-notation-v2.png, egress-policy-matrix-v1.xlsx

Can you route this to whoever owns plane demarcation on Redwood's side? We're aiming to lock the notation by EOD Friday so our network diagrams can be circulated to colo ops.

Forwarding Samira's diagram — TelcoGrid wants confirmation on two things: control/data plane attachment pattern (esp. sidecar/KV cache and control plane auth paths) and our recommended notation for egress behaviour.

My preliminary notes:
- Control plane appears centralised in a management subnet with a dedicated mTLS brokering path — good for cert propagation but we need to validate certificate distribution latency for canaries.
- Data plane shows tenant runtimes with sidecar proxies; they expect direct egress for telemetry to a dedicated observability endpoint and proxy egress for customer‑facing outbound.

Marissa / Kim / Neha / Jonas — can each of you call out one area you want explicitly annotated in the diagram (e.g., KV cache affinity, cert rotation path, NAT hairpin prevention, observability egress path)? I'll consolidate and send back to Samira.

I attached the files Samira sent for quick reference.

On Tue, Mar 2, 2026 at 10:03 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Samira's diagram — TelcoGrid wants confirmation on two things...

Thanks — quick comments below (I referenced the figure numbers on Samira's PNG).

1) KV cache affinity: annotate the data plane path from tenant runtime -> local KV cache (same AZ pod) and add fallback to cross‑rack replica only for cold start. We should explicitly label "prefer local kv" to avoid misrouting.

2) Control plane auth: show explicit controlplane -> customer KMS handshake (one‑way outbound TLS) and add a note: "no inbound controlplane admin access from customer networks". This avoids ambiguity for compliance.

3) Egress notation: replace the current green arrow for telemetry with a dashed arrow + label "telemetry (observability) — dedicated egress to telemetry endpoint (UDP/TCP)"; add a table inline mapping arrow style -> enforcement mechanism (NSG/NAT/proxy).

4) NAT hairpin prevention: add a small callout to show DNAT rules at the colo edge that prevent hairpin routing when tenant IPs map to public egress addresses.

I'll assemble a 1‑page markup and propose the exact SVG notation tomorrow morning. Action: Dylan, can you confirm if we need to call out HA pairs for sidecar proxies (active/standby) or if the sidecars are expected to be symmetric and loadbalanced?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Private Deploys — Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC: plane interface contracts + egress notation — consolidated response and next steps

Samira / team — thanks for the diagram and for the quick reviews. Below is a consolidated response; I'm copying the revised attachment names we uploaded to the shared Drive.

Summary of confirmations and edits (see Drive diagram for inline markups):
- KV cache affinity: we will annotate "prefer local KV" and include fallback replica path. This keeps latency predictable for streaming inference.
- Sidecar behaviour: sidecars should be symmetric and loadbalanced by the local dataplane router (no active/standby required). We'll add an explicit note that sidecars expose a health endpoint for LB checks.
- Control plane auth path: confirmed — control plane initiates mTLS to customer KMS endpoints for cert validation; no inbound admin paths from customer networks.
- Egress notation/table: updated notation (dashed = telemetry dedicated egress, solid = customer outbound via proxy, dotted = restricted/forbidden). Added enforcement column (NSG / NAT / proxy) in the matrix.
- NAT hairpin prevention: added colo edge DNAT callout and explicit BGP next‑hop annotation to avoid mis‑routing.

Attachments uploaded to Drive: vpc-plane-interface-notation-v2_annotated.png, egress-policy-matrix-v1_resolved.xlsx
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cVPChandoff (same folder; we added the revised files).

Next steps / action items:
- TelcoGrid (Samira) to confirm the observability endpoint IP ranges and any UDP port constraints (action: Samira, by Fri 3/6).
- Jonas / Kim to run through cert distribution latency hypothesis against Canary timing and report if we need an alternate cert propagation model (action: Jonas, Kim — EOD Thu 3/5).
- Marissa to ship the SVG notation spec for the operations diagram (action: Marissa — Tue 3/9).

If there are no further clarifications, I will mark the notation locked after Samira confirms the telemetry ranges.

Thanks all —
Dylan
